preamble: Fronting of the close back rounded vowel [u] to the near-close near-front rounded [ʏ]. In Icelandic, Old Norse short u became the vowel now written u and transcribed /ʏ/, as in Old Norse gull 'gold' > gull [ˈkʏtl̥] and sumar 'summer' > sumar [ˈsʏːmar], while Old Norse long ú stayed back and is now Icelandic /u/ (hús 'house'). The Old Norse article's table of vowel developments gives Old Norse u > Icelandic ʏ(ː), against Faroese ʊ/uː and Swedish ɵ/ʉː. The History of Icelandic article adds that Icelandic short vowels became lax, and that word-final -r gained an epenthetic /ʏ/ written u (Old Icelandic akr > akur). Wikipedia's Icelandic phonology cites Volhardt (2011) for a near-close [ʏ] and Flego & Berkson (2020) for a central vowel closer to [ʉ̞]; the traditional symbol ʏ is kept here as in the other Icelandic cells.

examples.note: Long [ʏː] in an open syllable: Icelandic vowel length now depends on syllable structure, not on Old Norse length.
Only the root vowel continues Old Norse u; the [ʏ] of the ending -ur is the epenthetic vowel added before final -r.
